measures.notes: EIA Updated Buildings Sector Equipment Costs 2023 (base 2022$), commercial rooftop heat pump tiers, Appendix A. Per-unit total installed cost, PRIMARY-EXTRACTED.

ACEEE Summer Study 2016 paper 3-345: VRF ~$18/ft2 vs code-min baseline $12-15/ft2 (PRIMARY-DOC/summary). low/high derived as a +/-3 spread around the reported $18/ft2 anchor (no explicit VRF-specific range in source) -- tuned-base band, flag for tightening against a real VRF-specific range.

SECONDARY sanity-band only (GeothermalFinder/EnergySage 2025-26 guides), office tier $4,500-7,500/ton (loop drilling = 50-70% of vertical closed-loop cost). EIA (2022$) and ORNL GeoVision (2019, ORNL/TM-2019/502) carry authoritative commercial GSHP figures, but a specific $/ton was not extracted from those PDFs in this pass -- flagged for ingest. source: tuned-base.

EIA 2023 study, base 2022$, centrifugal/screw/scroll chillers, $440-1390/ton total installed across capacity/efficiency tiers, PRIMARY-EXTRACTED. Underlying per-unit values are derived from proprietary RSMeans 2023 + Guidehouse; citing only EIA's published aggregation (public domain).

SECONDARY trade sanity band (Oxmaint 2026), mid-size commercial condensing boiler (1-3 MMBtu) installed cost. EIA carries an authoritative per-unit boiler figure in its Appendix A ('Commercial Gas-Fired Boilers'), but the specific $/unit was not extracted in this pass -- flagged for ingest. source: tuned-base.

PNNL-21944 (Oct 2012, DOE Contract DE-AC05-76RL01830), office-building scenario: maximum installed controller cost per packaged unit yielding a 3-yr payback, $1,560-2,990/RTU, PRIMARY-EXTRACTED. These are 'max acceptable for 3-yr payback' figures, not mean market bid prices -- treat as an upper-bound-anchored band; retail-building tier ($4,180-8,390/RTU) was not seeded separately.

LBNL (Mills, Building Commissioning: A Golden Opportunity, 2009), existing-buildings RCx: median ~$0.30/ft2, range $0.05-0.40/ft2, PRIMARY-DOC/summary, 2009$. ~16% energy savings, payback ~1.1yr reported alongside.

LBNL Mills & Sartor, Energy Use and Savings Potential for Laboratory Fume Hoods (OSTI 862161, 2006): CAV->VAV retrofit ~$6,000/hood, mid-2000s $, PRIMARY-DOC/summary; retrofit kits reported at 10-20% of a new hood's cost. low/high derived as a +/-20% band around the reported $6,000 anchor (source gives a single point figure) -- tuned-base band.

DOE Building America, Cost Analysis of Roof-Only Air Sealing and Insulation Strategies: roof air-seal+insulation to R-20 ~$10.25-20/ft2 roof area, PRIMARY-DOC/summary. Source scope is RESIDENTIAL; applied here as a commercial tuned-base proxy pending a commercial-specific envelope survey. Base year is not explicitly stated in the source; a conservative 2015 Building America-era vintage is assumed pending verification -- flag.

SECONDARY trade guide (HireElectrical / National Efficiency Supply 2026), commercial LED retrofit $0.50-5.00/ft2. No authoritative redistributable commercial LED $/ft2 survey was found in this research pass (DOE SSL/CALiPER, GSA Green Proving Ground, and utility TRMs are flagged for future ingest). source: tuned-base.

SECONDARY trade guide (eilitetech), example 75HP VFD install $12k-18k implies ~$160-240/HP. The $80-250/HP figure elsewhere in the source is a utility prescriptive REBATE, not an install cost, and was deliberately excluded. No authoritative installed-cost survey was found; DOE UMP Ch.18 is an M&V protocol, not a cost source. source: tuned-base.

CED Engineering, HVAC -- Guide to Demand Control Ventilation (course monograph, PRIMARY-DOC/summary): DCV adds ~$1-3/cfm of outside air; CO2 sensors now <$200 (was >$500 a decade ago). Base year not stated in source; conservatively dated 2015 pending verification -- flag. ERV/HRV per-unit costs ($4k-20k+/unit, SECONDARY sanity band only, no clean $/cfm survey) were not seeded separately; utility TRMs (IL, CA DEER, NY) are the recommended authoritative substitute per the research doc.

In-unit multifamily 240V heat-pump water heater (45-55 gal, UEF 3.3), installed. NESCAUM/Energy Solutions 2024, base 2023$, US-average (index-100) rows: equipment $1,837 (CA eTRM) + labor $1,314 = installed $3,152 WITHOUT panel upgrade (low/base); WITH panel upgrade installed $5,427 (high). Panel-upgrade adder ~$2,275 (TECH Clean CA; NV5 $2,000-4,500 band) hits only ~8% of SF installs but more often in older NE stock -- carried as the high bound. Regionalize via region arg (state spread is labour-driven). Source is residential single-family; applied to in-unit MF equipment of equivalent size. Incremental vs gas/electric storage ~+$2,270-2,290. source: primary-extracted.

In-unit multifamily 120V plug-in heat-pump water heater (65 gal, UEF ~3.2), installed. NESCAUM/Energy Solutions 2024, base 2023$, US-average row: equipment $2,630 (NBI) + labor $762 = installed $3,392. NO panel upgrade needed (plug-in 120V) and faster install (~4 hr vs 6.95 hr for 240V) -- hence flat low/base/high; equipment is costlier than 240V (larger tank + integrated mixing valve). State installed range $3,149 (VA) - $3,804 (NY); use region arg to regionalize. Residential SF source applied to in-unit MF. source: primary-extracted.

Ducted split unitary air-source heat pump (whole-unit heating+cooling, normalized 65 kBtu/h), installed. NESCAUM/Energy Solutions Oct-2024, base 2024$, Table 20 US-average cells: low $9,392 (existing ductwork, no panel upgrade); base $11,179 (new distribution, no panel -- typical off gas furnace/baseboard); high $13,530 (new distribution + panel upgrade). Cheapest whole-unit HP option. Panel adder ~$2,351, new-duct adder ~$4,500; existing-ductwork retrofit gets ~40% labour discount. Residential whole-home source applied to in-unit / townhome / small-building MF. source: primary-extracted (OCR of image table).

Ducted packaged unitary air-source heat pump (65 kBtu/h), installed. NESCAUM/Energy Solutions Oct-2024, base 2024$, Table 20 US-average: low $10,216 (existing duct, no panel); base $12,002 (new dist, no panel); high $14,353 (new dist + panel). ~$800 above split unitary. Same distribution/panel adders as split unitary. Residential whole-home source applied to in-unit/small-building MF. source: primary-extracted (OCR of image table).

Ducted single-zone mini-split air-source heat pump (65 kBtu/h), installed. NESCAUM/Energy Solutions Oct-2024, base 2024$, Table 20 US-average: low $13,546 (existing duct, no panel); base $15,333 (new dist, no panel); high $17,684 (new dist + panel). Breakdown from MassCEC single-zone mini-split actuals. Residential whole-home source applied to in-unit MF. source: primary-extracted (OCR of image table).

Ductless 3-zone mini/multi-split air-source heat pump (65 kBtu/h), installed -- the dominant in-unit MF retrofit where no ductwork exists. NESCAUM/Energy Solutions Oct-2024, base 2024$, Table 20 US-average: no-panel $15,818 (low/base -- ductless has no ductwork variability), with-panel $18,170 (high). Slightly above ducted single-zone due to more zones. Breakdown from MassCEC multi-split actuals. Residential whole-home source applied to in-unit MF. source: primary-extracted (OCR of image table).

Air-to-water heat pump with low-temp hydronic distribution (65 kBtu/h), installed -- relevant to MF/central hydronic buildings converting off gas/oil boilers. NESCAUM/Energy Solutions Oct-2024, base 2024$, Table 21 US-average: low $52,252 (existing hydronic, no panel); base $56,060 (new low-T distribution, no panel -- typical, existing high-T loops need conversion); high $58,411 (new dist + panel). Emerging tech, high cost expected to fall as US manufacturing scales. Confidence LOW: OTR-calc vs MassCEC actual disagree ~$10k on equipment (OTR $24.2k vs MassCEC $9.1k); MassCEC total was ~$42k vs OTR ~$57k -- wide band retained. source: primary-extracted (OCR of image table).
